merger_description:
Australian Metal Recycling Network Pty Ltd (**AMRN**), a wholly owned subsidiary of Sims Limited (**Sims**), proposes to acquire the business assets of OneStop Metal Recycling (Tas) Pty Ltd (**OneStop**) (the **Acquisition**).

Sims and OneStop are both engaged in the acquisition, processing and sale of ferrous and non-ferrous scrap metal in Tasmania. Sims currently operates a scrap metal recycling facility at Bell Bay, north of Launceston. OneStop operates facilities at Glenorchy in southern Tasmania (Hobart) and Cooee on the north-west coast (Burnie).

The assets to be acquired comprise the operating business conducted by OneStop, including its Glenorchy and Cooee sites, together with plant and equipment, inventory, business contracts, intellectual property, goodwill and other assets used in the operation of the business.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) has considered the
information provided with the notification waiver application, and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Act.
Based on the information provided in the application, including the
parties’ revenue in Australia, the ACCC considers that, if the
Acquisition were put into effect, the notification thresholds would be
met.
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC is unable to
reach a view that the Acquisition would not be likely to raise
competition issues in any market based on the information provided,
given:
a. there is horizontal overlap between Sims and OneStop in the
acquisition of ferrous and non-ferrous scrap metal and the
supply of processed ferrous and non-ferrous scrap metal in
Tasmania
b. the parties’ combined share in the acquisition of ferrous and
non-ferrous scrap metal and the supply of processed ferrous
and non-ferrous scrap metal may be significant
c. there is uncertainty regarding the level of competitive
constraint likely to be exerted from alternative acquirers of
ferrous and non-ferrous scrap metal and suppliers of
processed ferrous and non-ferrous scrap metal in Tasmania.
The ACCC considers that these potential competition issues warrant
consideration through the notification process, including via
consultation with third parties.
Given the above, the ACCC has determined not to make the
notification waiver determination applied for.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
